title: Why We Hold on to Things

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Ryan Staten is opening up a storage unit in Austin, Texas.
sentences.zh: 瑞安·斯塔滕正在得克萨斯州奥斯汀市租下一间储物间。

sentences.en: I'm trying to make as much room as possible.
sentences.zh: 我正尽量腾出尽可能多的空间。

sentences.en: It's 10 feet by 5 feet with steel walls.
sentences.zh: 这里长10英尺，宽5英尺，四周是钢制墙壁。

sentences.en: I'm unloading my mom's stuff.
sentences.zh: 我在卸我妈的东西。

sentences.en: Ryan's mom recently moved out of town and left her things with him.
sentences.zh: 瑞安的母亲最近搬到了外地，把东西留给了他。

sentences.en: It's just crap to me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说这些就是垃圾。

sentences.en: Lots of files she thought she would need.
sentences.zh: 很多她以为自己以后会用到的文件。

sentences.en: lots of purses
sentences.zh: 很多钱包

sentences.en: probably like
sentences.zh: 大概有

sentences.en: 10 purses
sentences.zh: 10个钱包

sentences.en: why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: why 10 purses?
sentences.zh: 为什么会有10个钱包？

sentences.en: I'm a firm believer
sentences.zh: 我坚信

sentences.en: in just shed your skin
sentences.zh: 应该褪去旧皮

sentences.en: get rid of it
sentences.zh: 摆脱它们

sentences.en: and start traveling light
sentences.zh: 开始轻装旅行

sentences.en: but then
sentences.zh: 然而

sentences.en: Ryan stops
sentences.zh: 瑞安停了下来

sentences.en: he's looking at a VHS tape
sentences.zh: 他正看着一盘录像带

sentences.en: turning it over in his hands
sentences.zh: 把它在手里翻来覆去地看

sentences.en: it's a recording of a TV show
sentences.zh: 这是他小时候

sentences.en: that he was on
sentences.zh: 参加过的一个

sentences.en: when he was a child
sentences.zh: 电视节目的录像

sentences.en: he shakes his head
sentences.zh: 他摇了摇头

sentences.en: It's so like his mom to do this.
sentences.zh: 这太符合他妈妈的作风了。

sentences.en: And there's sentimental value, so it's hard to get rid of.
sentences.zh: 而且这些东西具有情感价值，所以很难丢弃。

sentences.en: She does it in abundance, just to like maybe make her feel better.
sentences.zh: 她买得实在太多了，可能只是为了让自己感觉好一点。

sentences.en: It's not just Ryan's mom.
sentences.zh: 不只是瑞安的妈妈这样。

sentences.en: It's hard for many people to let go of their stuff.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，放手自己的物品都很艰难。

sentences.en: That's because the things we own can be imbued with deep meaning.
sentences.zh: 这是因为我们拥有的东西被赋予了深层的意义。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, the complex psychology of what it means to own something
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》将探讨拥有的真正含义背后复杂的心理学

sentences.en: and how our possessions reveal a great deal about us.
sentences.zh: 以及我们的物品如何深刻地揭示了我们自己。

sentences.en: When you move to a new home or a new city, you take your things with you.
sentences.zh: 当你搬进新家或来到新城市时，你会把东西随身带走。

sentences.en: As you carry box after box out of your house, you might have an epiphany.
sentences.zh: 当你把一个又一个箱子搬出房子时，你可能会突然顿悟。

sentences.en: You own a lot of stuff.
sentences.zh: 你拥有太多东西了。

sentences.en: Bruce Hood is the author of Possessed, Why We Want More Than We Need.
sentences.zh: 布鲁斯·胡德是《着迷：我们为什么渴望拥有更多》一书的作者。

sentences.en: He's a psychologist at the University of Bristol.
sentences.zh: 他是布里斯托大学的心理学家。

sentences.en: He explores the psychology of ownership.
sentences.zh: 他专门研究所有权的心理学。

sentences.en: He knows the answer to the question you may have asked yourself during your last move.
sentences.zh: 他知道你在上次搬家时可能问过自己的那个问题的答案。

sentences.en: Why do I own so much stuff?
sentences.zh: 为什么我会有这么多东西？

sentences.en: Bruce Hood, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 布鲁斯·胡德，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: You mentioned, Bruce, that there are about 50,000 storage facilities in the United States.
sentences.zh: 布鲁斯，你提到美国大约有5万个储物设施。

sentences.en: There are even more storage facilities than Starbucks cafes or McDonald's restaurants.
sentences.zh: 储物设施的数量甚至比星巴克咖啡馆或麦当劳餐厅还要多。

sentences.en: What does this reveal about how much stuff we have, Bruce?
sentences.zh: 布鲁斯，这说明了我们有多少东西？

sentences.en: It's amazing, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这太惊人了，对吧？

sentences.en: It's a really strange phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常奇怪的现象。

sentences.en: And it's fairly recent, I would imagine,
sentences.zh: 而且我想这相当晚近，

sentences.en: as a consequence of the fact that our productions have increased as our manufacturing has really developed over the last couple of centuries.
sentences.zh: 这是过去几个世纪我们的制造业真正发展起来、产量增加的结果。

sentences.en: But we seem to be increasingly on this relentless pursuit of more and more things.
sentences.zh: 但我们似乎越来越无休止地追求越来越多的东西。

sentences.en: And that's really what drove me to start writing a book about what's the motivation behind it all.
sentences.zh: 这正是促使我开始写一本书去探讨这一切背后的动机的原因。

sentences.en: Yeah, what's interesting is that we don't just own stuff, but we often find ourselves bewildered that we own so much stuff,
sentences.zh: 是的，有趣的是，我们不仅拥有东西，而且我们常常发现自己对拥有这么多东西感到困惑，

sentences.en: almost as if we didn't have agency in acquiring all the stuff ourselves.
sentences.zh: 就好像我们在获取所有这些东西的过程中根本没有主导权一样。

sentences.en: So we look around us and we say,
sentences.zh: 所以我们环顾四周，然后说：

sentences.en: how could I possibly have collected all the stuff around me?
sentences.zh: 我怎么可能收集了我周围所有的这些东西？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, that's kind of the reasoning behind the title of the book, Possessed.
sentences.zh: 对，这其实就是本书书名《着迷》（Possessed）背后的逻辑。

sentences.en: And it's a play on words because, you know,
sentences.zh: 这是一个双关语，因为你知道的，

sentences.en: obviously possessions are the things that we own.
sentences.zh: 很显然，财产就是我们拥有的东西。

sentences.en: But I'm also alluding to the fact that it's almost as if
sentences.zh: 但我也在暗示这样一个事实：

sentences.en: there's a sort of little demon inside us
sentences.zh: 就好像我们内心住着一个小恶魔

sentences.en: which is compelling us to go for more and more things.
sentences.zh: 它在强迫我们去追求越来越多的东西。

sentences.en: It's like this irrational little monster who controls our consumption.
sentences.zh: 就像这个控制我们消费的无理取闹的小怪兽。

sentences.en: I understand people have studied how much stuff we have in the context of studying fire hazards.
sentences.zh: 据我了解，人们曾在研究火灾隐患的背景下研究过我们拥有多少东西。

sentences.en: So obviously, the more stuff you have, the more stuff you have that's combustible.
sentences.zh: 很显然，你拥有的东西越多，其中易燃物品就越多。

sentences.en: And you've cited an amazing statistic in your book.
sentences.zh: 你在书中引用了一个惊人的统计数据。

sentences.en: In the last 30 years, the time to what is called spontaneous combustion has gone down from 28 minutes to 4 minutes.
sentences.zh: 在过去30年里，发生所谓自燃的时间从28分钟缩短到了4分钟。

sentences.en: What is this telling us, Bruce?
sentences.zh: 布鲁斯，这说明了什么？

sentences.en: Well, we've got too many flammable things in our house.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们屋里的易燃物品太多了。

sentences.en: But it's literally just too many things that we're accumulating.
sentences.zh: 但说白了，就是我们囤积的东西太多了。

sentences.en: And in fact, a lot of the stuff we have, we overspill into our garages.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们的很多东西都堆到了车库里。

sentences.en: Most garages these days don't contain the cars anymore.
sentences.zh: 如今大多数车库里都不再停放汽车了。

sentences.en: They're on the sidewalk.
sentences.zh: 汽车都停在马路边上。

sentences.en: People are literally moving.
sentences.zh: 人们真的在不断腾挪。

sentences.en: They fill one room, and then they have to put it into the garage to fill it up.
sentences.zh: 他们填满了一个房间，然后不得不把东西塞进车库直到塞满。

sentences.en: So yeah, that combustion time is just a reflection of the amount of things which can catch fire, which has increased significantly.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，那个起火时间只是反映了能够起火的物品数量显著增加。

sentences.en: I want to play you a clip from the comedian George Carlin,
sentences.zh: 我想给你听一段喜剧演员乔治·卡林的音频片段，

sentences.en: who had a joke about the real purpose of all our homes.
sentences.zh: 他曾开玩笑说过我们所有房屋的真正目的。

sentences.en: That's the whole meaning of life, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这不就是生活的全部意义吗？

sentences.en: Trying to find a place for your stuff.
sentences.zh: 努力为你的东西找个地方放。

sentences.en: That's all your house is.
sentences.zh: 这就是你房子的全部作用。

sentences.en: Your house is just a place for your stuff.
sentences.zh: 你的房子不过是存放东西的地方。

sentences.en: If you didn't have so much goddamn stuff, you wouldn't need a house.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有那么多该死的东西，你根本不需要房子。

sentences.en: You could just walk around all the time.
sentences.zh: 你大可以随时随地四处走动。

sentences.en: That's all your house is.
sentences.zh: 这就是你的房子的全部意义。

sentences.en: It's a pile of stuff with a cover on it.
sentences.zh: 它不过是一堆盖着屋顶的杂物。

sentences.en: You see that when you take off in an airplane,
sentences.zh: 当你坐飞机起飞时就能看到这一点，

sentences.en: and you look down and you see everybody's got a little pile of stuff.
sentences.zh: 当你往下看，你会发现每个人都有一小堆东西。

sentences.en: Everybody's got their own pile of stuff.
sentences.zh: 每个人都有属于自己的那一堆东西。

sentences.en: That's so true.
sentences.zh: 太对了。

sentences.en: So, Bruce, you know, I remember a time in my life when I felt like all my worldly possessions not only fit in a single room, but they fit comfortably inside a single room.
sentences.zh: 所以，布鲁斯，我记得我生命中曾有这样一段时期，当时我觉得我所有的身家不仅能塞进一个房间，而且在一个房间里放得很宽敞。

sentences.en: When I look around my home today, if I put all my stuff in one room, I probably wouldn't be able to breathe.
sentences.zh: 但如果今天环顾我的家，如果把我所有的东西都堆在一个房间里，我可能连气都喘不过来。

sentences.en: Is that the same for you, Bruce?
sentences.zh: 布鲁斯，你也是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, we generally upsize our houses when we get kids, especially when you get children.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们通常会在有了孩子后换更大的房子，尤其是有了小孩之后。

sentences.en: and you suddenly find yourself buying a whole lot of things that you never knew existed.
sentences.zh: 你会突然发现自己买了一大堆你以前闻所未闻的东西。

sentences.en: As we go through different stages of life, we just seem to accumulate more and more.
sentences.zh: 随着我们经历不同的人生阶段，我们似乎只是在不断囤积更多东西。

sentences.en: And getting rid of it is really a bit of a challenge.
sentences.zh: 而要摆脱它们确实是个不小的挑战。

sentences.en: That's something I've found very difficult.
sentences.zh: 我发现这也是一件非常难的事。

sentences.en: Although I think in the States, you guys often got yard sales.
sentences.zh: 不过我认为在美国，你们经常会办庭院旧货出售。

sentences.en: So maybe it's a cultural thing with a bit of variation.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能是一种带有少许差异的文化现象。

sentences.en: But yeah, invariably, you accumulate more and more things.
sentences.zh: 但不管怎样，你不可避免地会囤积越来越多的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, although the yard sales are a way of transferring the junk inside your home to the junk inside my home.
sentences.zh: 是的，尽管庭院旧货出售只是把摆在你家里的垃圾转移到我家里的垃圾的一种方式。

sentences.en: Basically buy someone else's junk.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是买别人的破烂。

sentences.en: We should just keep our own junk and then not bother with the art sale.
sentences.zh: 我们其实应该保留自己的破烂，然后就别费心思搞什么旧货出售了。

sentences.en: You're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 你完全说对了。

sentences.en: I want to get to our propensity to own stuff, the psychology of it.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈我们拥有物品的倾向，以及背后的心理学。

sentences.en: But I want to start with a simpler idea that you alluded to actually a second ago.
sentences.zh: 但我先从一个更简单的想法开始，你刚才其实也提到了这一点。

sentences.en: 200 years ago, people owned a lot less stuff than we do today.
sentences.zh: 200年前，人们拥有的东西比今天要少得多。

sentences.en: What is the role of the industrial revolution in producing all the stuff that we see in our lives today?
sentences.zh: 工业革命在我们生活中看到的所有物品的生产过程中扮演了什么角色？

sentences.en: It's really interesting when you think about the amount of time it would have taken to make a very common household item, say a chair, for example.
sentences.zh: 仔细想想制造一件非常普通的家居用品（比方说一把椅子）需要花费多少时间，这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: I mean, there would have been skilled craftsmen who would turn the lace and make the wood and glue it together.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，过去会有熟练的工匠车削木料、制作木件并将其粘合在一起。

sentences.en: And it could have taken them quite a bit of time to do that.
sentences.zh: 他们可能需要花相当长的时间才能完成。

sentences.en: But when we developed the Industrial Revolution, we had machinery, we had lathes that were driven by water wheels initially, and then we had steam-powered machinery.
sentences.zh: 但当我们迎来了工业革命，我们有了机械，我们有了最初由水车驱动的车床，后来又有了蒸汽动力机械。

sentences.en: And so one person, rather than taking a day, could start to produce literally tens of chairs and then eventually hundreds of chairs with mechanization.
sentences.zh: 因此，通过机械化，一个人不再需要花上一天时间，而是可以开始生产几十把椅子，最后甚至能生产数百把椅子。

sentences.en: And so what happened was this exponential rise in productivity.
sentences.zh: 于是发生的情况就是生产力的呈指数级增长。

sentences.en: People migrated from the countrysides into the cities to fill the factories, and the factories started to generate more and more products.
sentences.zh: 人们从乡村涌入城市填满工厂，而工厂开始生产越来越多的产品。

sentences.en: And, of course, the profit margin lines started to decrease, so they had to sell more and more things.
sentences.zh: 当然，利润率开始下降，所以他们必须卖出越来越多的东西。

sentences.en: And so what I think was a perfect storm, if you like, of the ability to produce more stuff, but also at the same time,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你愿意的话，我认为这是一场完美的风暴：既有生产更多物品的能力，但在同时，

sentences.en: people who are really kind of working upon our psychology to make us want to buy more and more things.
sentences.zh: 还有人在我们的心理上做文章，让我们渴望购买越来越多的东西。

sentences.en: So as you just indicated, you know, the Industrial Revolution produced a lot of stuff and marketers have gotten very skilled at selling the stuff to us.
sentences.zh: 正如你刚才所指出的，工业革命生产了大量的物品，营销人员也非常擅长把这些东西卖给我们。

sentences.en: But they didn't actually produce the desires that we have in the first place.
sentences.zh: 但他们实际上并没有凭空创造出我们最初拥有的欲望。

sentences.en: In your book, you tell the evocative story of the sinking of a ship called the Royal Charter in 1859.
sentences.zh: 你在书中讲述了一个引人入胜的故事，关于1859年皇家宪章号（Royal Charter）货轮的沉没。

sentences.en: It was returning to Liverpool from Australia.
sentences.zh: 它当时正从澳大利亚返回利物浦。

sentences.en: Tell me what happened on the ship, Bruce.
sentences.zh: 布鲁斯，请讲讲船上发生了什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, this was a remarkable story.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个非同寻常的故事。

sentences.en: As you say, it was a ship returning from the goldfields of Australia.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，这是一艘从澳大利亚金矿返回的船。

sentences.en: And it sank off the coast of north of Wales just on its return to Liverpool.
sentences.zh: 就在它返回利物浦的途中，在北威尔士海岸附近沉没了。

sentences.en: But what makes the story more tragic in many ways is that this was not inevitable
sentences.zh: 但在许多方面，让这个故事更具悲剧色彩的是，这场悲剧并非不可避免，

sentences.en: because many of the people who drowned were the miners who wouldn't relinquish the gold that they
sentences.zh: 因为许多溺水身亡的矿工都不肯舍弃他们

sentences.en: had so feverishly worked for.
sentences.zh: 费尽千辛万苦才淘来的黄金。

sentences.en: They had it sewn into their coats and they wore money belts and
sentences.zh: 他们把金子缝进大衣里，系着钱带，

sentences.en: they wouldn't abandon it.
sentences.zh: 死也不肯抛弃它们。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, the extra weight just pulled them to their death.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，额外的重量最终把他们拽向了死亡。

sentences.en: So I think that story just reveals that we can become very irrational when it comes to giving
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这个故事恰恰表明，在舍弃我们的财产这件事上，

sentences.en: up our possessions.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会变得非常不理性。

sentences.en: In this case, gold is notoriously turns men into fools.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，黄金可以说是出了名地能把人变成傻子。

sentences.en: Our insatiable hunger to own things remains ever-present today.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们对拥有的无餍渴求依然无处不在。

sentences.en: And increasingly, as more of our lives are spent online,
sentences.zh: 而且随着我们的生活越来越多地在线上度过，

sentences.en: the possessions that we desire don't even need to be tangible iteMs.
sentences.zh: 我们渴望的财富甚至不需要是有形的物品。

sentences.en: Bruce cites an unusual club that sold in 2010 for $635,000.
sentences.zh: 布鲁斯举了一个不寻常的例子：一个俱乐部在2010年以63.5万美元的价格售出。

sentences.en: It was called Club Never Die.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“永不消亡俱乐部”（Club Never Die）。

sentences.en: Well, this is a remarkable story,
sentences.zh: 这是一个非同寻常的故事，

sentences.en: which really reveals the way that our attitudes to possessions don't necessarily have to be physical possessions.
sentences.zh: 它确实揭示了我们对待财产的态度不一定非得是实体财产。

sentences.en: They can be concepts, they can be thoughts, they can be ideas.
sentences.zh: 它们可以是概念，可以是思想，也可以是创意。

sentences.en: And I'm talking about the world of online gaming.
sentences.zh: 我指的是网络游戏的世界。

sentences.en: And Club Never Die was a virtual club where you could buy virtual iteMs.
sentences.zh: “永不消亡俱乐部”是一个虚拟俱乐部，你可以在其中购买虚拟物品。

sentences.en: To be more precise, it was a virtual club on a virtual asteroid in a virtual universe.
sentences.zh: 更准确地说，它是虚拟宇宙中虚拟小行星上的一个虚拟俱乐部。

sentences.en: People were really immersed in this whole gaming world.
sentences.zh: 人们真正沉浸在这个完整的游戏世界里。

sentences.en: But effectively, they were paying good money for virtual objects.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，他们是在花大钱购买虚拟物品。
